subject: Fwd: Post-AGI Alpha Hunt — Reality-State Infrastructure, Fab Activation & Negative-Data Moats
executive_summary: This run produced three genuinely new primitives rather than another list of AI hardware suppliers:

theses.title: *Fab activation latency* — owning a lithography/tool slot is
theses.body: 1. *Fab activation latency* — owning a lithography/tool slot is economically useless until the physical site, cleanroom and utilities are ready.

theses.title: *World-state consistency infrastructure* — increasingly capable
theses.body: 2. *World-state consistency infrastructure* — increasingly capable agents need an authoritative, continuously updated representation of what actually exists in the physical world.

theses.title: *Failure-history / negative-data moats* — autonomous scientists
theses.body: 3. *Failure-history / negative-data moats* — autonomous scientists explicitly improve by remembering unsuccessful directions; data that humans historically discard can become the most defensible training asset. The highest-alpha public-company rabbit holes are *Takasago Thermal Engineering (1969.T)* and *VusionGroup (VU.PA <http://VU.PA>)*. The most important non-stock research branch is the *humanoid fail-passive gap*, because it identifies a new safety-hardware category rather than merely more certification spending.

theses.title: FAB ACTIVATION LATENCY — 9.4/10 Thesis
theses.body: 1. FAB ACTIVATION LATENCY — 9.4/10 Thesis The semiconductor bottleneck is migrating from *tool availability* toward *the ability to turn purchased tools into qualified production capacity*. ASML’s FY2026 guidance explicitly says customer readiness to receive systems — including fab completion and cleanroom availability — is a major determinant of the wide revenue range. That is unusually direct evidence that the scarce object is becoming *activated cleanroom capacity*, not just equipment. Micron’s Hiroshima expansion illustrates the time mismatch: a ¥1.5tn AI-memory project is adding ~28,000 m² of cleanroom, yet equipment move-in is not scheduled until H2 2028. Intelligence/design cycles can compress dramatically; certified physical manufacturing space cannot. Candidate exposure: Takasago Thermal Engineering (1969.T) Japanese HVAC / environmental-engineering specialist with direct relevance to high-spec industrial facilities. FY ended Mar-2026 revenue rose 11.1% to ¥423.9bn while operating profit jumped 47.3%; orders exceeded ¥460bn. Market cap is roughly ¥0.57–0.64tn depending source/date. This is not a pure semiconductor name, which is precisely why it is interesting: if high-spec cleanroom/environmental engineering becomes the gating layer, earnings can inflect before the narrative catches up. New kernel variable activation_latency = time(tool_committed -> qualified_output) And: stranded_tool_risk = committed_equipment_value × probability(site_not_ready) Caveat The earnings surge is already visible, and Japan construction inflation/labor constraints can compress margins. Exposure is diversified rather than pure-play. Falsifier If fab/cleanroom completion stays consistently ahead of WFE deliveries and ASML/customer commentary stops citing site readiness as a delivery constraint, downgrade the thesis. Evidence: ASML FY2026 commentary; Micron Hiroshima groundbreaking and cleanroom timetable; Takasago FY2026 results.

theses.title: WORLD-STATE CONSISTENCY INFRASTRUCTURE — 9.2/10 Thesis
theses.body: 2. WORLD-STATE CONSISTENCY INFRASTRUCTURE — 9.2/10 Thesis Post-AGI agents can reason over digital information nearly instantly, but they cannot act correctly if the digital representation of reality is stale. That creates a new scarce commodity: *authoritative physical state.* Examples: what product is physically on a shelf, its actual price, which asset revision is installed, whether a machine is available, whether a component has moved, whether inventory exists, whether an instrument is calibrated. The investment implication is subtle: the value can accrue not to the agent but to the *sensor/identity/update layer that continuously reconciles digital world models with atoms*. Candidate exposure: VusionGroup (VU.PA) VusionCloud now manages *>500 million connected electronic shelf labels*, versus ~220m one year earlier. H1 2026 adjusted revenue grew 29% organically; recurring value-added-services revenue grew 73%, with annualized recurring VAS revenue up 83%. This network is interesting beyond electronic price tags. It is effectively a giant installed mesh linking physical retail locations to cloud state. In an agentic-commerce world, machine-readable, continuously synchronized shelf state becomes much more valuable. Current valuation screens are surprisingly moderate after the selloff: roughly €2bn market cap and ~17x 2026 forward earnings / ~11x 2027 estimates depending source. Why this is different from ordinary IoT IoT measures things. *World-state consistency infrastructure settles disagreements between the digital model and physical reality.* Kernel edge: digital_claim --verified_by--> physical_state New feature: state_decay_rate = probability(digital representation becomes wrong per unit time) The faster the physical environment changes, the more valuable low-latency synchronization becomes. Caveats H1 order intake was down 22% YoY despite improving sequentially. ESLs also face political/regulatory backlash around dynamic pricing; U.S. state restrictions could

theses.title: NEGATIVE-DATA MOATS — 9.0/10 conceptual alpha Fresh evidence
theses.body: 3. NEGATIVE-DATA MOATS — 9.0/10 conceptual alpha Fresh evidence The March 2026 *EvoScientist* paper does something economically important: its persistent memories explicitly record *unsuccessful research directions* so future agents avoid repeating failed experiments. The authors report improved idea quality and code-execution success versus seven open/commercial AI-scientist systems. This supports a stronger formulation of our negative-data thesis: As model intelligence commoditizes, proprietary records of what *doesn’t work under specific real conditions* become disproportionately valuable. Humans systematically discard this information because journals reward successful results. Autonomous systems do the opposite: failed trajectories reduce future search cost. New metric negative_information_value = avoided_future_experiment_cost × probability(agent_would_repeat_failure) And: failure_capture_ratio = recorded_failed_trials / actual_failed_trials A company with mediocre positive-data IP but near-complete failure histories may possess a better AI-era moat than a company with a clean publication corpus. Tradable exposure No convincing pure-play public exposure yet. Avoid forcing one. The better alpha hunt is to identify industries where experiments are expensive and failure logs remain proprietary: semiconductor process recipes, specialty chemicals, aerospace qualification, biologics process development, battery formation, industrial catalysts. Falsifier If frontier models infer unsuccessful regions accurately enough from positive observations/physics that explicit failure histories provide little incremental improvement, the moat collapses.

theses.title: HUMANOID FAIL-PASSIVE GAP — 8.9/10
theses.body: 4. HUMANOID FAIL-PASSIVE GAP — 8.9/10 This is a material refinement of the earlier certification-bandwidth thesis. An August 2026 paper argues industrial humanoids have a structural safety problem: conventional machine safety assumes that removing power moves equipment toward a safe state. For a balancing biped, removing power can *cause an uncontrolled fall*. That means classical safety components do not cleanly transfer. The paper can certify the external safety chain but localizes the unresolved problem to the robot-side reaction chain / balancing controller. Investment implication Humanoid deployment may create an entirely new hardware stack: - safety-rated active stabilization - redundant actuation/power paths - safety-rated compute - fail-operational motor control - controlled-energy braking - independent balance sensing - validated low-latency safety networking The alpha is therefore not just TÜV/SGS certification. It is *new safety BOM per robot*. Candidate exposure Novanta (NOVT) is worth monitoring because it sells precision motion/control components and its robotics/automation bookings have been strong, but valuation is already demanding (~36–39x forward earnings; ~29x EV/EBITDA on current screens). Siemens/ABB provide less convex but broader safety-control exposure. Falsifier If mechanical architectures evolve so humanoids naturally collapse into passive safe states, or regulators accept software-only safety cases without redundant hardware, the incremental safety BOM is much smaller.

theses.title: SIMULATION SUCCESS CREATES A REALITY-CALIBRATION TAX — 8.6/10
theses.body: 5. SIMULATION SUCCESS CREATES A REALITY-CALIBRATION TAX — 8.6/10 Recent work on interactive robot world models reports policies trained on generated interactions performing comparably to policies trained with equivalent real-world data, with simulation and real-world performance strongly correlated. At first glance this destroys experimental scarcity. The second-order implication is more interesting: *cheap synthetic experience increases the marginal value of the comparatively tiny stream of real-world observations needed to verify that the simulator remains correct.* As simulation volume approaches infinity: value(real calibration sample) ↑ especially around rare failures, deformable materials, wear, contamination, human interaction and novel environments. This suggests a barbell: - abundant synthetic training data becomes cheap; - sparse, high-integrity physical edge-case data becomes expensive. That links back to Samsara/Vusion-style physical telemetry, autonomous-lab traces, industrial condition monitoring and robot fleet data. Falsifier If foundation world models generalize across physical distribution shifts with negligible ongoing real-world calibration, the reality-calibration tax falls sharply.
